items.title: Bukit Aman: Six to be charged over RM7m Petaling Jaya kidnapping tomorrow as two suspects become prosecution witnesses
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, July 26 — Six men will be charged tomorrow over the RM7 million ransom kidnapping in Petaling Jaya after police completed their investigation into the case, while two other suspects have been released to become prosecution witnesses. Bukit Aman Criminal Investigation Department director Comm Datuk M. Kumar said in a statement that the investigation paper into the case, reported on July 17, was referred to the Attorney General’s Chambers on July 24, which subsequently directed that charges be brought against the six suspects. The six are due to appear before the Petaling Jaya Sessions Court at 9.30am tomorrow.

items.title: Sabah Immigration denies viral claim of Filipino detainee deaths at depot
items.summary: KOTA KINABALU, July 26 — The Sabah Immigration Department has denied a viral claim alleging that many Filipino detainees had died due to overcrowding at the state’s immigration detention depots. State Immigration director Datuk SH Sitti Saleha Habib Yussof said that the allegation was false, baseless and misleading. “All Filipino detainees housed at the Immigration detention depots in Sabah are in good condition while awaiting repatriation to their home country,” she said in a statement today.

items.title: Aminuddin challenges opposition to prove PH left development agenda unfinished
items.summary: PORT DICKSON: Datuk Seri Aminuddin Harun has hit back at opposition leaders claiming they want to resume an unfinished development agenda under the Pakatan Harapan state administration. The Negri Sembilan PH chairman challenged his rivals to present factual evidence of any project or plan that had allegedly stalled during PH's five-year tenure leading the state. He was responding to Barisan Nasional chairman Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi, who denied that BN was copying PH's manifesto, claiming instead that BN sought to continue a development agenda that had been interrupted.

items.title: German police hunt suspect after deadly car ramming near Berlin Gay Pride
items.summary: BERLIN: German police searched on Sunday for a suspect believed linked to Islamist circles after a car ploughed into a crowd near Berlin's Gay Pride celebrations, killing one person and wounding 16 others. A suspect, believed to have links to "Islamist circles" had been "identified" but not yet arrested, police spokesman Florian Nath said. "A vehicle entered the Tiergarten park and hit several people," police said.

items.title: Defence Ministry identifies asset procurements for G2G execution, says Khaled
items.summary: Defence Minister Datuk Seri Mohamed Khaled Nordin said the approach would enable Malaysia to secure competitive pricing while providing greater assurance of supply. "Several countries, including Italy and France, have also proposed conducting procurement through G2G arrangements." Khaled said several criteria were applied in selecting Malaysia's G2G partners for asset procurements.

items.title: Zahid dismisses speculation of early general election
items.summary: TAMPIN: There have been no discussions on the possibility of an early general election, said Deputy Prime Minister Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi. Responding to speculation that the next general election could be called ahead of schedule following claims of a growing "Blue Wave" in support of BN, Zahid said no such matter had been raised within the Unity Government. "In the Unity Government, there are 18 parties, including five coalition blocs.

items.title: Ahead of 60th anniversary, King’s royal diplomacy elevates Russia-Malaysia ties, says ambassador
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, July 26 — The royal diplomacy of Malaysia’s King, Sultan Ibrahim, has brought the people of Russia and Malaysia closer despite the geographical distance between the two countries, while elevating bilateral ties to a new sphere, Russian Ambassador to Malaysia Naiyl Latypov said. Praising His Majesty's royal approach, Latypov said the King's diplomacy has elevated Russia-Malaysia bilateral ties as the two countries prepare to mark the 60th anniversary of diplomatic relations next year. "Russia highly appreciates His Majesty’s royal diplomacy.

items.title: Six to be charged tomorrow over RM7mil PJ kidnapping
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Six men will be charged tomorrow over the kidnapping of a man for a RM7 million ransom in Petaling Jaya earlier this month. Bukit Aman Criminal Investigation Department director Datuk M. Kumar said police have completed investigations into eight suspects linked to the July 17 case. He said investigation papers were submitted to the Attorney-General's Chambers on July 24, which subsequently directed that six men be charged under Section 3(1) of the Kidnapping Act 1961.

items.title: Former PM Muhyiddin says it should be PAS exiting Perikatan, not Bersatu
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, July 26 — Bersatu president Muhyiddin Yassin has pushed back against calls for his party to leave Perikatan Nasional (PN), arguing that PAS — not Bersatu — should be the one to step away from the coalition after choosing to end political cooperation between the two parties. FMT reported Muhyiddin saying said Bersatu, as a co‑founder of PN, could not be forced out of the coalition and retained every right to remain. PAS ended its cooperation with Bersatu early last month, though both remain PN components.

items.title: [UPDATED] 12 policemen arrested over alleged RM2mil extortion of Chinese citizen
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Twelve policemen of various ranks have been arrested for allegedly extorting RM2 million from a Chinese citizen. Sources said the victim was released after paying US$140,000 (about RM560,000) to the suspects. The victim later lodged a report at the Dang Wangi district police headquarters, prompting an internal investigation.

items.title: Muhyiddin breaks silence on Bersatu turmoil, alleges plot to remove him
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Bersatu president Tan Sri Muhyiddin Yassin has spoken out on the party's leadership crisis, claiming former deputy president Datuk Seri Hamzah Zainudin sought to remove him. Muhyiddin said attempts to replace him as Bersatu president began after he stepped down as prime minister, but he remained in the position after receiving unanimous support from delegates at the party's annual general assembly in 2023. He said he had initially intended to retire as party president but agreed to continue serving for one final term after members rejected his decision.

items.title: RCI on Tabung Haji won't sway Negri Sembilan voters, says Zahid
items.summary: TAMPIN: The government's move to release the Royal Commission of Inquiry (RCI) report on Tabung Haji will not affect voter sentiment in the Negri Sembilan election on Aug 1. Zahid said he supported the prime minister's intention to disclose the report and declassify it from the Official Secrets Act (OSA). "The report must be declassified from the Official Secrets Act (OSA)," he said.

items.title: Residents cash in on Dubai real estate cooldown amid Mideast war
items.summary: DUBAI: Just over a year after moving to Dubai, Steve found himself moving unexpectedly up the property ladder, taking advantage of a cooling real estate market amid the Middle East war. His new apartment is larger and closer to work than his previous resident, but the rent is nonetheless 15 per cent cheaper, he said, using a pseudonym due to Dubai's sensitivity on the matter. "Since the war, the market's shifted from a seller's market to a buyer's market," she said.

items.title: Sabah Immigration denies viral claim of Filipino detainee deaths in overcrowded depots
items.summary: KOTA KINABALU: The Sabah Immigration Department has refuted social media claims alleging that numerous Filipino detainees died due to overcrowding at the state's detention depots. State Immigration director Datuk SH Sitti Saleha Habib Yussof said the allegations were false, baseless, and misleading, adding that a viral photograph linked to the claim was not taken at any immigration detention depot in Sabah. "All Filipino detainees housed at the immigration detention depots in Sabah are in good condition while awaiting repatriation to their home country," she said in a statement today.

items.title: Malaysia remains Scoot's key market on robust travel demand: Chief commercial officer
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysia remains a key market for Scoot, the low-cost carrier of the Singapore Airlines (SIA) Group, driven by sustained demand for leisure and business travel, the airline's chief commercial officer Calvin Chan said. He said Scoot now serves 12 destinations in Malaysia, mounting 130 weekly flights between both countries. These factors have combined to generate strong demand for air travel between Malaysia and Singapore, he said.

items.title: Mohamad Hasan says non-Malays have ‘no reason to be unduly worried’ by BN-Perikatan pact in Negeri Sembilan
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, July 26 — Barisan Nasional (BN) has assured non-Malay voters they will not be sidelined if the coalition secures victory in the upcoming Negeri Sembilan state election, despite its cooperation with Perikatan Nasional (PN). According to The Star , BN deputy president Datuk Seri Mohamad Hasan said claims by rivals that minorities would be marginalised were unfounded, stressing that BN remained the dominant force in the partnership. He added that seven of BN’s seats had been allocated to MCA and two to MIC, while PN was also fielding non-Muslim candidates.

items.title: Malaysian agritech startup Qarbotech expands global footprint
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysian agritech startup Qarbotech is expanding its global footprint, with its technology, QarboGrow, a carbon quantum dot-based photosynthesis enhancer, now being used by nearly 7,500 farmers worldwide. Qarbotech co-founder and chief executive officer Chor Chee Hoe said QarboGrow recorded nearly RM3 million in sales last year, with a large share generated from overseas markets. Chor said the company is conducting pilot trials in Japan, with prospective customers considering purchases if the trials are successful.

items.title: Fahmi: Students need patriotism, digital literacy to navigate modern challenges
items.summary: JEMPOL: Secondary school students must be continuously nurtured with patriotism and equipped with digital literacy to face modern challenges. Communications Minister Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil said an emphasis on nationhood and history is crucial to ensuring every citizen understands their responsibility in advancing the country. He said this after meeting 60 Form Six students following a dialogue session held in conjunction with the Pentarama X Kelab Malaysiaku programme and the Safe Internet Campaign at the Jempol District Information Office today.

items.title: Online extremists exploit lonely youths' search for friendship, belonging
items.summary: He said NVE particularly affected younger people facing psychological stress, bullying, social isolation or emotional struggles, with social media, video games and other online platforms providing avenues for exposure and influence. Ahmad said that unlike groups such as the Islamic State which use religious or political narratives to justify violence, NVE was driven largely by psychological factors and personal discontent. He said repeated exposure to content that normalised violence could influence how individuals processed emotions and perceived violent behaviour.

items.title: Malaysian students breathe easier as Australia spares Asean neighbours from visa fee surge
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, July 26 — Australia has imposed a sharp 25 per cent rise in international student visa fees but carved out an exemption for applicants from Asean nations, including Malaysia, as part of efforts to deepen regional ties. “A reduced visa fee rate for students from Asean nations reflects the importance Australia places on welcoming high quality students from South-east Asia,” Assistant Minister for International Education Julian Hill told Singapore’s The Straits Times (ST). Australia already applies lower fees for Pacific nations, including Timor Leste, which joined Asean in October 2025, as part of its diplomatic outreach.

items.title: PN-BN pact puts Negri Sembilan people's interests above differences, says Samsuri
items.summary: The PN chairman said this was demonstrated through the coalition's supplementary offers, which were designed to complement the manifesto presented by BN for the state election. "PN has presented 14 additional offers centred on six key areas, namely administration, youth and family, economy, welfare, education, and employment. Yesterday, PN launched 14 additional offers across six core pillars under the theme 'PN Sepakat Hebatkan Negeri Sembilan' ahead of the state election.

items.title: Australia exempts Asean students from visa fee hike in bid to deepen regional ties
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Australia has carved out an exemption for students from Asean nations after raising its international student visa fee by 25 per cent. "A reduced visa fee rate for students from Asean nations reflects the importance Australia places on welcoming high-quality students from Southeast Asia," he said. Australia already maintained a lower fee of A$745 for students from Pacific nations, including Timor-Leste, which joined Asean in October 2025, as part of its diplomatic outreach to the region.

items.title: Trump faces midterm reckoning with 100 days to US vote
items.summary: WASHINGTON: One hundred days before the US midterm elections, President Donald Trump's Republicans are staring down polling that points to the loss of the House of Representatives and a ferocious battle to retain the Senate. A Democratic House would give the party control of powerful committees and subpoena authority, likely subjecting Trump's administration to two years of investigations and potentially exposing him to a third impeachment drive. US elections website Decision Desk HQ predicts that the Democratic Party has a 59-per cent chance of winning the House, forecasting a 224-211 majority.

items.title: Rescuers scour South China Sea for 23 missing after Vietnamese vessel sinks
items.summary: HONG KONG: Rescuers were searching for 23 people missing after a Vietnamese ship sank in the busy waterway of the South China Sea, while 39 were pulled from the waters, China's state broadcaster CCTV said. Authorities in the southern province of Hainan said the cargo vessel Khoi Nguyen 18, with 62 Vietnamese nationals aboard, ran into distress in waters near Fiery Cross Reef, CCTV added. A distress flare from the vessel was first spotted by a Chinese rescue ship, the Nanhai Jiu 115, on Saturday evening, CCTV said.

items.title: Aeon's legal setback unlikely to hurt operations: MBSB Research
items.summary: The appellate court upheld the High Court's decision ordering Aeon to pay Betanaz Properties Sdn Bhd RM18.68 million plus interest, while dismissing Betanaz's larger RM59.3 million claim. Aeon's counterclaim against Betanaz and Ahmad Zaki Resources Bhd was also dismissed. Assuming interest accrues at five per cent a year, MBSB Research estimated additional interest of about RM1.4 million from Jan 23, 2025 to July 2026.

items.title: Higher Sara allocation could ease cost pressures, says expert
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: A higher Sumbangan Asas Rahmah (Sara) allocation could provide immediate relief to lower-income households grappling with rising living costs, but the assistance should remain a temporary safety net rather than a long-term solution. "Direct assistance such as Sara can provide immediate relief by helping families manage essential expenses, especially food and daily necessities. The Sara assistance is channelled through recipients' MyKad, allowing eligible individuals to purchase essential goods.

items.title: Penang sees rise in consumer claims as awareness of redress rights grows
items.summary: BUKIT MERTAJAM: Consumer awareness in Penang of the right to seek redress through the Tribunal for Consumer Claims Malaysia (TTPM) is on the rise, with the number of claims filed showing an upward trend in recent years. Domestic Trade and Cost of Living Ministry Penang director S. Jegan said 614 claims were filed in 2024, rising to 777 cases last year, while 444 claims were recorded in the first six months of this year as of June 30. However, he acknowledged that some consumers are still unaware that they can bring disputes involving compensation claims before the TTPM without going through complicated court proceedings.

items.title: Strong winds and rain lash China after Typhoon Noul makes landfall
items.summary: BEIJING: Typhoon Noul made landfall in China early Sunday morning, state media reported, lashing a stretch of the southern coast with strong winds and rain in the fiercest storm to hit the country this year. The centre of the typhoon crossed over land at around 3:50 am (1950 GMT) near the town of Pinghai, Guangdong Province – about 80 kilometres northeast of financial hub Hong Kong – state broadcaster CCTV reported. "Noul is moving steadily into inland Guangdong and weakening progressively, but gales are still affecting many places over Hong Kong, with occasional storm force winds over high ground," the Hong Kong Observatory said.

items.title: BN rejects racial rhetoric, insists NS polls cooperation won't alter party's stance
items.summary: In a statement today, BN secretary-general Datuk Seri Dr Zambry Abd Kadir said the coalition remained committed to its principles despite its political understanding forged for the state polls. "BN remains steadfast in standing by its own principles," he said. Zambry said BN's strength lay in its multiracial power-sharing model, which had helped develop Malaysia for more than six decades through mutual respect, moderation and political stability.

items.title: Kerjaya's data centre win opens door to more M&E jobs, says Kenanga
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Kerjaya Prospek Group Bhd's recent subcontract win for a data centre project in the Klang Valley could pave the way for more mechanical and electrical (M&E) jobs in the fast-growing sector, Kenanga Research said. Kerjaya's unit, Kerjaya Prospek (M) Sdn Bhd, secured a RM52.5 million lump-sum subcontract for civil, structural and basic low-voltage M&E works involving a new 275-kilovolt consumer landing station serving a data centre in the Klang Valley. The latest contract lifts Kerjaya's year-to-date job wins to RM2.15 billion, close to Kenanga Research's full-year target of RM2.3 billion.

items.title: Tok Mat defends BN's record on Indian community
items.summary: He said among the key measures was a housing policy for estate workers forced to leave plantations following changes in the sector. Mohamad said the state government had developed dedicated housing areas to ensure affected workers continued to have a place to live. "We introduced a housing policy specifically for estate workers.

items.title: Nadma: Disaster victims can claim cash aid up to four times a year
items.summary: JERTIH, July 26 — Malaysians affected by disasters are eligible to receive the Bantuan Wang Ihsan (BWI) up to four times a year, subject to the claim conditions set by the National Disaster Management Agency (Nadma). Nadma Community and Social Development Section director Jefny Muhammad said the assistance is provided to ease the burden of victims affected by disasters such as floods, landslides, fires, tidal waves and other calamities. Jefny said 108,000 heads of household nationwide received BWI amounting to RM108 million during the 2025/2026 Northeast Monsoon season.

items.title: BN pledges no assessment tax hike in Negri Sembilan for 5 years
items.summary: Mohamad said the state government should not rely on higher taxes to increase revenue but instead generate income through development. "We want to increase the state's revenue, but not by taxing the people. Development will generate revenue, not taxing the people," he said.

items.title: Housewife loses RM119,599 to Facebook investment scam
items.summary: KOTA TINGGI, July 26 —A housewife lost RM119,599.24 after falling victim to an investment scam on July 19. Kota Tinggi police chief Supt Yusof Othman said the 58-year-old woman came across an advertisement for an investment scheme, identified as XM Royal, on Facebook. Yusof said the victim realised she had been scammed after failing to receive the promised investment returns despite making several payments.

items.title: Woman loses nearly RM120,000 in non-existent investment scheme
items.summary: KOTA TINGGI: A 58-year-old woman lost nearly RM120,000 after being duped by a non-existent investment scheme promising returns of RM15,000 within two hours. District police chief Superintendent Yusof Othman said police received a report regarding the incident on Thursday. Yusof said the victim made eight money transfer transactions into eight different bank accounts, totalling RM119,599.24.

items.title: Tawau floods: 335 victims still at relief centre
items.summary: KOTA KINABALU: A total of 335 flood victims from 96 families remain at a temporary relief centre in Tawau as of 8am today, with no casualties or untoward incidents reported so far. The Sabah State Disaster Management Committee Secretariat said all victims are still taking shelter at the Tawau Sports Complex Multipurpose Hall. The victims are residents from Kampung Tanjung Batu Keramat, Tanjung Batu Darat, Tanjung Batu Otentik and Kampung Kinabutan Tiku Batu 6.

items.title: Sanusi's statement reflects Pas tendency to divide people, says Fahmi
items.summary: JEMPOL: Kedah Menteri Besar Datuk Seri Muhammad Sanusi Md Nor's statement on racial issues reflects the Pas leadership's tendency to play up racial sentiments and divide society, says Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil. The Pakatan Harapan communications director said such politics should not be practised, urging politicians instead to promote unity and respect the country's diversity. "His statement reflects a widespread attitude within Pas.

items.title: CPO futures seen lower next week on profit taking after recent rally
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Crude palm oil (CPO) futures on Bursa Malaysia Derivatives are expected to trade lower next week as profit-taking is likely to emerge after the recent rally despite crude oil prices remaining elevated. Interband Group of Companies senior palm oil trader Jim Teh said CPO futures had climbed to about RM4,700 per tonne alongside crude oil prices, which reached about US$100 per barrel, prompting speculative buying. The November 2026 contract advanced RM123 to RM4,753 per tonne, December 2026 increased RM116 to RM4,779 per tonne, and January 2027 improved RM103 to RM4,800 per tonne.

items.title: Temporary shelters house families in flood-stricken Melaka Tengah and Jasin
items.summary: MELAKA, July 26 —The number of flood victims in Melaka rose to 124 people from 37 families as of 8 am today, with three temporary relief centres still operating in Melaka Tengah and Jasin. In Melaka Tengah, 55 victims from 17 families are taking shelter at the Pantai Kundor Japerun Hall. while 44 victims from 12 families are placed at SK Serkam Darat and 25 victims from eight families at SK Bukit Tembakau in Jasin.

items.title: Scammer poses as government official, contractor loses over RM50,000
items.summary: KUALA TERENGGANU, July 26 — A 52-year-old electrical wiring contractor lost RM50,400 after falling victim to a fake government tender offer scam. Kuala Terengganu police chief ACP Azli Mohd Noor said the victim received an email on July 14 containing a quotation request for the installation of solar LED street lights purportedly under a special local authority allocation. “The victim, who believed the offer was genuine, made two payments totalling RM50,400 to two separate bank accounts on July 23 using business funds.

items.title: PM Anwar attends Citrawarna 2026 launch and cultural parade
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, July 26 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim attended the opening ceremony and parade of Citrawarna 2026 at Dataran Merdeka yesterday, a flagship Tourism Malaysia event held as part of the Visit Malaysia 2026 (VM2026) campaign. He was joined by Tourism, Arts and Culture Minister Datuk Seri Tiong King Sing, Deputy Minister Chiew Choon Man, Chief Secretary to the Government Tan Sri Shamsul Azri Abu Bakar and Tourism Malaysia director-general Mohd Amirul Rizal Abdul Rahim. Supported by Kuala Lumpur City Hall (DBKL), Warisan Kuala Lumpur, the National Department for Culture and Arts (JKKN), Istana Budaya and the National Textile Museum, Citrawarna 2026 aims to promote Malaysia’s arts, culture and heritage tourism to domestic and international visitors.

items.title: Police detain man for assaulting Ipoh officer issuing compound notice
items.summary: IPOH, July 26 — Police have detained a man to assist investigations into an incident in which an Ipoh City Council enforcement officer was assaulted and threatened while issuing a compound notice at Jalan Pengkalan Barat 35 yesterday. Ipoh district police chief ACP Muhammad Najib Hamzah said the 42-year-old suspect allegedly acted aggressively by trying to hit the officer with a vehicle, tailing him, pulling his shirt collar and making threats. “Acting on information, a team of officers from the Ipoh District Police Headquarters Criminal Investigation Department detained the suspect today at about 12.40 pm to assist investigations.

items.title: Raja Muda of Selangor, wife, welcome first child, Tengku Alia Amira
items.summary: SHAH ALAM, July 26 — The Raja Muda of Selangor, Tengku Amir Shah Sultan Sharafuddin Idris Shah and his wife Datin Paduka Seri Afzaa Fadini Abdul Aziz yesterday announced the birth of their first child, Tengku Alia Amira Tengku Amir Shah. Tengku Amir Shah and Datin Paduka Seri Afzaa Fadini were married in a royal solemnisation ceremony at Masjid Istana Diraja, Istana Alam Shah, Klang, on Oct 2, 2025. The royal couple was solemnised by Selangor Mufti Datuk Dr Anhar Opir, witnessed by Tengku Panglima Raja Selangor Tengku Ahmad Shah Alhaj and Tengku Indera Pahlawan Diraja Tengku Datuk Setia Putra Alhaj in the private wedding ceremony.

items.title: BN chairman defends manifesto as original and improved, dismisses ‘copying’ accusations
items.summary: PORT DICKSON, July 26 — Barisan Nasional (BN) chairman Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi has rejected allegations that BN’s manifesto, launched yesterday, was copied from those of other parties. The Umno president said the manifesto built on BN’s existing agenda and had been refined to meet current requirements. Early voting for the Negeri Sembilan state polls will take place this Tuesday, with polling day scheduled for Aug 1.

items.title: Third flood relief centre opens in Melaka as number of evacuees rises
items.summary: MELAKA, July 26 — The third temporary relief centre has been opened in Melaka to accommodate the increasing number of flood victims as of 8 pm yesterday. The Melaka State Disaster Management Committee Secretariat said the third relief centre opened is at Sekolah Kebangsaan (SK) Bukit Tembakau at 3.15pm yesterday. Three areas in Jasin are affected, namely Kampung Pulai, Kampung Serkam and Kampung Bukit Tembakau.

items.title: PM Anwar demands swift action on Felda initiatives amid settler frustration
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, July 26 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim wants the seven initiatives announced earlier to help Federal Land Development Authority (Felda) settlers implemented without further delay. Anwar said he has requested progress reports on all initiatives, which include assistance to Felda and new generation housing, to be provided every month so that their implementation is not delayed. On July 7, the Prime Minister announced seven initiatives in conjunction with Felda Settlers’ Day and 70th Anniversary celebration, including strengthening digital literacy for settlers involving an allocation of RM15.85 million to 317 eligible Felda schemes.

items.title: Malaysians in Qatar urged to follow security advisories, avoid military areas
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, July 26 — Malaysians in Qatar have been advised to follow security instructions issued by the local authorities and avoid military areas following the latest developments in the Gulf region. The Embassy of Malaysia in Doha also urged Malaysians to remain vigilant, stay alert to their surroundings, and avoid being influenced by or spreading false information and rumours. The embassy also advised Malaysians to check the latest flight schedules before travelling from Qatar and to ensure their personal and family information are kept up to date.

items.title: Perikatan launches Negeri Sembilan election manifesto with six main pillars
items.summary: SEREMBAN, July 26 — Perikatan Nasional (PN) today launched its manifesto outlining six main pillars for the 16th Negeri Sembilan State Election. The manifesto, with the theme ‘PN Sepakat Hebatkan Negeri Sembilan’, was launched by PN chairman Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Samsuri Mokhtar. For the latest updates on the 16th Negeri Sembilan State Election, visit https://prn.bernama.com/n9.

items.title: For nearly a century, this Penang family in Jelutong has let the sun make its soy sauce
items.summary: Today, brothers Kam Kam Yoon, 87, and Kam Pak Yuen continue running San Kwan Loong Soy Sauce Factory using the same natural fermentation method their mother brought from China when the family business was established almost 100 years ago. “We still make our soy sauce using natural fermentation under the sun,” he said. Kam Kam Yoon took over the San Kwan Loong soy sauce factory business at 19 years old.

items.title: Three secondary school students in Ampang detained over bullying incident
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, July 25 — Police have arrested three male secondary school students near here on suspicion of beating another student at a block of flats in Ampang. Ampang Jaya District Police Chief ACP Khairul Anuar Khalid said that during the incident at 12.31 pm yesterday, the victim was taken to the bottom of a staircase at a block in Flat Sri Nilam, Ampang, by a male student before being struck on the face and body by the suspects. Earlier, a 3-minute and 29-second video showing a male student being beaten by another student went viral on social media, having been filmed by a third individual.

items.title: Autistic girl dies in 13th-floor apartment fall in Kuala Terengganu
items.summary: Kuala Terengganu police chief ACP Azli Mohd Noor said the department received a call around 7.50 am reporting a young girl lying in the sixth-floor parking area, believed to have fallen from a 13th-floor window. “The victim was pronounced dead at the scene by a medical officer from Hospital Sultanah Nur Zahirah (HSNZ),” he said in a statement today. He said the victim’s mother realised her daughter was missing only after another resident informed her at around 7am.

items.title: Anwar says there is a need to reconstruct history to the Malaysian narrative
items.summary: He said history must not be dictated by the country’s former colonial masters, whether it is the United Kingdom, Japan or the United States. “It must be determined by our people and reconstructed to give meaning to the level of sacrifice and devotion of the people of Penang,” he said at the official opening of Fort Cornwallis after restoration works on the colonial monument. He said it is not necessarily erasing history but a fact that there is a different narrative behind the monuments left behind by the country’s former colonial masters.

items.title: Education groups Dong Zong and Jiao Zong decry PAS president Hadi Awang’s ‘pendatang’ remarks
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, July 25 — Two of Malaysia’s largest Chinese education advocacy groups, Dong Zong and Jiao Zong, have issued a strong joint condemnation of PAS president Tan Sri Abdul Hadi Awang’s recent remarks labelling DAP supporters as “pendatang” (immigrants) and accusing some Malay Muslims of being “ungrateful” and “colluding” with others. In a joint statement released today, the duo—collectively known as Dong Jiao Zong—warned that such rhetoric undermines the national identity by defining citizenship along ethnic and religious lines, while distorting healthy political competition into inter-ethnic hostility. They said the remarks not only fail to strengthen national unity but also risk eroding the longstanding trust built among Malaysia’s diverse communities.

items.title: Former PM Najib undergoes coronary procedure; no stent needed, doctors confirm
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, July 25 — Former Malaysian Prime Minister Datuk Seri Najib Razak is in stable condition and recovering after undergoing a coronary angiogram today, with doctors confirming that no further surgical intervention, such as balloon angioplasty or stent implantation, is required. According to a statement released by his legal counsel, Messrs Shafee & Co., the medical procedure was deemed necessary following a series of health evaluations over the past several weeks. The medical team had previously advised that there was an estimated 95% probability that Najib would require further intervention.

items.title: Police launch 16 probes into alleged election-related offences in Negeri Sembilan
items.summary: SEREMBAN, July 25 — Negeri Sembilan police have received 16 reports and opened 11 investigation papers, including two opened yesterday, over alleged election-related offences in the state polls. Negeri Sembilan police chief Datuk Alzafny Ahmad said one investigation paper opened yesterday was under Section 435 of the Penal Code for committing mischief by fire, resulting in the loss or damage of property. However, Alzafny said the security and public order situation throughout the election process remained good and under control.

items.title: Family, including baby, rescued from Tanjung Kling flash floods
items.summary: Melaka Fire and Rescue Department (JBPM) public relations officer Mohd Hafidzatullah Rashid said seven firefighters from the Tangga Batu Fire and Rescue Station were deployed after the department received an emergency call at 9.47am. Meanwhile, Melaka Civil Defence Force (APM) director Lt Col (PA) Kamarulsyah Muslim said continuous heavy rain since 1 am caused several flood-prone areas in Melaka Tengah to be inundated. Kamarulsyah, who is also the State Disaster Management Committee (JPBN) Secretariat spokesperson, said no temporary relief centre had been opened and no victims evacuated as of 10 am.

items.title: Negeri Sembilan cooperation with Perikatan does not bind BN, says Ahmad Maslan
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, July 25 — Barisan Nasional’s cooperation with Perikatan Nasional in the Negeri Sembilan state election is only a political understanding and does not amount to a formal agreement, Umno Supreme Council member Datuk Seri Ahmad Maslan said. According to Utusan Malaysia , Ahmad said there was no formal pact at the state level, leaving Umno and BN free to determine the strategies they considered best to remain relevant and win the election. “At the state level, there is no agreement.

items.title: Suspect arrested in Shah Alam for armed van heist attempt
items.summary: South Klang district police chief ACP Lim Jit Huey said the remand application for the local suspect in his 20s, was made at the Klang Court yesterday. “The court then granted the suspect a six-day remand starting yesterday until July 29,” he said via a Whatsapp message today. Earlier, Bukit Aman Criminal Investigation Department (CID) director Datuk M Kumar said the local suspect, in his 20s, was arrested in Shah Alam, Selangor at 11 am, July 23.

items.title: Melaka floods: Emergency shelters set up after relentless rain
items.summary: MELAKA, July 25 —Two temporary relief centres have been opened after heavy rain caused flooding in several areas in the Melaka Tengah and Jasin districts as of 3 pm today. Continuous heavy rain since early this morning has caused flooding in several areas in Melaka Tengah, namely Kampung Lereh, Peringgit, Kampung Bachang, Kampung Kolam Limbongan, Tengkera, Bukit Rambai, Tanjung Kling, Pengkalan Perigi and Kampung Berlian. In Jasin, the affected villages are Kampung Pulai, Kampung Serkam and Kampung Bukit Tembakau.

items.title: Calls for Malays to unite must go on, Sanusi’s speech taken out of context, says Annuar Musa
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, July 25 — Calls by leaders for Malays to unite, remain united and love their homeland must continue, Tan Sri Annuar Musa said today as he defended Kedah Menteri Besar Datuk Seri Muhammad Sanusi Md Nor over remarks that have drawn criticism for their racial tone. In a Facebook post, Annuar said Sanusi’s remarks had been taken out of context and denied that the PAS leader had intended to hurt the feelings of other ethnic communities in Malaysia. That is completely untrue.” he said.
